# Book I, Proposition 26

*Two angles and one side make the remaining sides equal*

[Euclid's proof](#euclids-proof) · [In Lean](#in-lean) · [What it rests on](#what-it-rests-on) · [Mishnah](#mishnah)

> If two triangles have the two angles equal to two angles respectively, and one side equal to one side, namely, either the side adjoining the equal angles, or that subtending one of the equal angles, they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides and the remaining angle to the remaining angle.

**In Lean:** ✅ proved, as Euclid states it · Euclid's argument

<p align="center"><em>Make two angles (blue and red) and the side between them (black) equal, and the other sides (red and blue) and the third angle (yellow) are equal too. An equal side opposite one of those angles serves as well.</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/26.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition I.26, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two angles ABC, BCA equal to the two angles DEF, EFD respectively, namely the angle ABC to the angle DEF, and the angle BCA to the angle EFD; and let them also have one side equal to one side, first that adjoining the equal angles, namely BC to EF;

I say that they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides respectively, namely AB to DE and AC to DF, and the remaining angle to the remaining angle, namely the angle BAC to the angle EDF.

For, if AB is unequal to DE, one of them is greater.

Let AB be greater, and let BG be made equal to DE; and let GC be joined.

Then, since BG is equal to DE, and BC to EF,

the two sides GB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively;

and the angle GBC is equal to the angle DEF;

therefore the base GC is equal to the base DF,

and the triangle GBC is equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the equal sides subtend; [I. 4]

therefore the angle GCB is equal to the angle DFE.

But the angle DFE is by hypothesis equal to the angle BCA;

therefore the angle BCG is equal to the angle BCA,

the less to the greater: which is impossible.

Therefore AB is not unequal to DE,

and is therefore equal to it.

But BC is also equal to EF;

therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively,

and the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF;

therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,

and the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]

Again, let sides subtending equal angles be equal, as AB to DE;

I say again that the remaining sides will be equal to the remaining sides, namely AC to DF and BC to EF, and further the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF.

For, if BC is unequal to EF, one of them is greater.

Let BC be greater, if possible, and let BH be made equal to EF; let AH be joined.

Then, since BH is equal to EF, and AB to DE,

the two sides AB, BH are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain equal angles;

therefore the base AH is equal to the base DF,

and the triangle ABH is equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the equal sides subtend; [I. 4]

therefore the angle BHA is equal to the angle EFD.

But the angle EFD is equal to the angle BCA;

therefore, in the triangle AHC, the exterior angle BHA is equal to the interior and opposite angle BCA:

which is impossible. [I. 16]

Therefore BC is not unequal to EF,

and is therefore equal to it.

But AB is also equal to DE;

therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain equal angles;

therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,

the triangle ABC equal to the triangle DEF,

and the remaining angle BAC equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

From [`Elements/BookI/Prop26.lean`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop26.lean). Euclid's sentences are the `--` comments, and our own notes are in `/- … -/`; the lines under each sentence are the Lean that carries it out.

```lean
/-- If two triangles have the two angles equal to two angles respectively, and one side equal to one
side, namely, either the side adjoining the equal angles, or that subtending one of the equal
angles, they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides and the remaining
angle to the remaining angle. -/
theorem Prop26 {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDEF : Triangle D E F)
    (hB : ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F) (hC : ∠ B C A = ∠ E F D)
    (hside : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∨ ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖) :
    ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖ ∧ ‖A C‖ = ‖D F‖ ∧ ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ ∧ ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F := by
  -- Let ABC, DEF be two triangles having the two angles ABC, BCA equal to the two angles DEF,
  -- EFD respectively, namely the angle ABC to the angle DEF, and the angle BCA to the angle
  -- EFD; and let them also have one side equal to one side, first that adjoining the equal
  -- angles, namely BC to EF;
  rcases hside with hBC | hAB
    -- I say that they will also have the remaining sides equal to the remaining sides
    -- respectively, namely AB to DE and AC to DF, and the remaining angle to the remaining
    -- angle, namely the angle BAC to the angle EDF.
    -- For, if AB is unequal to DE, one of them is greater.
  · /- The argument for the greater side works with the triangles named either
       way round. We write it once and exchange them below. -/
    have greater : ∀ {A B C D E F : Point}, Triangle A B C → Triangle D E F →
        ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F → ∠ B C A = ∠ E F D → ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ →
        ‖D E‖ < ‖A B‖ → False := by
      intro A B C D E F hABC hDEF hB hC hBC hlt
      -- Let AB be greater, and let BG be made equal to DE; and let GC be joined.
      /- I.3 supplies the cut and says explicitly that G is between B and A. -/
      obtain ⟨G, hBGA, hBG⟩ := Prop3 hDEF.ne₁₂ (by rwa [len_symm B A])
      obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hABC.ne₁₂
      have hG_AB := on_line_of_between_ends hBGA hB_AB hA_AB
      have hBGC : Triangle B G C := Triangle.of_line hB_AB hG_AB
        (ne_of_between hBGA) (hABC.off_line hA_AB hB_AB)
      obtain ⟨GC, hG_GC, hC_GC⟩ := Postulate1 G C hBGC.ne₂₃
      -- Then, since BG is equal to DE, and BC to EF,
      -- the two sides GB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively;
      have hBG_ED : ‖B G‖ = ‖E D‖ := hBG.trans (len_symm D E)
      -- and the angle GBC is equal to the angle DEF;
      have hGBC : ∠ G B C = ∠ D E F :=
        (angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between hBGA) hABC.ne₂₃.symm).trans hB
      -- therefore the base GC is equal to the base DF,
      obtain ⟨hGC, harea, hG, hC'⟩ := Prop4 hBGC hDEF.bac hBG_ED hBC hGBC
      -- and the triangle GBC is equal to the triangle DEF,
      have : △ G B C = △ D E F := by
        rw [area_swap G B C, area_rotate G C B, area_swap D E F, area_rotate D F E]
        exact harea
      -- and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the
      -- equal sides subtend; [I. 4]
      have : ∠ B G C = ∠ E D F ∧ ∠ B C G = ∠ E F D := ⟨hG, hC'⟩
      -- therefore the angle GCB is equal to the angle DFE.
      have hGCB : ∠ G C B = ∠ D F E :=
        (angle_symm hBGC.ne₂₃ hBGC.ne₁₃).trans
          (hC'.trans (angle_symm hDEF.ne₂₃ hDEF.ne₁₃))
      -- But the angle DFE is by hypothesis equal to the angle BCA;
      have hDFE : ∠ D F E = ∠ B C A :=
        (angle_symm hDEF.ne₁₃ hDEF.ne₂₃).trans hC.symm
      -- therefore the angle BCG is equal to the angle BCA,
      have hBCG : ∠ B C G = ∠ B C A :=
        (angle_symm hBGC.ne₁₃ hBGC.ne₂₃).trans (hGCB.trans hDFE)
      -- the less to the greater: which is impossible.
      have hless := angle_lt_of_between hABC (between_symm hBGA)
      rw [← angle_symm hBGC.ne₁₃ hBGC.ne₂₃,
        ← angle_symm hABC.ne₂₃ hABC.ne₁₃, hBCG] at hless
      exact lt_irrefl _ hless
    -- Therefore AB is not unequal to DE,
    -- and is therefore equal to it.
    have hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖ := by
      rcases lt_trichotomy ‖A B‖ ‖D E‖ with hlt | heq | hgt
      · exact False.elim (greater hDEF hABC hB.symm hC.symm hBC.symm hlt)
      · exact heq
      · exact False.elim (greater hABC hDEF hB hC hBC hgt)
    -- But BC is also equal to EF;
    -- therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively,
    -- and the angle ABC is equal to the angle DEF;
    have hBA_ED : ‖B A‖ = ‖E D‖ :=
      (len_symm B A).trans (hAB.trans (len_symm D E))
    -- therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,
    obtain ⟨hAC, -, hA, -⟩ := Prop4 hABC.bac hDEF.bac hBA_ED hBC hB
    -- and the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]
    exact ⟨hAB, hAC, hBC, hA⟩
    -- Again, let sides subtending equal angles be equal, as AB to DE;
    -- I say again that the remaining sides will be equal to the remaining sides, namely AC to DF
    -- and BC to EF, and further the remaining angle BAC is equal to the remaining angle EDF.
    -- For, if BC is unequal to EF, one of them is greater.
  · /- Again either triangle may have the greater side. -/
    have greater : ∀ {A B C D E F : Point}, Triangle A B C → Triangle D E F →
        ∠ A B C = ∠ D E F → ∠ B C A = ∠ E F D → ‖A B‖ = ‖D E‖ →
        ‖E F‖ < ‖B C‖ → False := by
      intro A B C D E F hABC hDEF hB hC hAB hlt
      -- Let BC be greater, if possible, and let BH be made equal to EF; let AH be joined.
      obtain ⟨H, hBHC, hBH⟩ := Prop3 hDEF.ne₂₃ hlt
      obtain ⟨BC, hB_BC, hC_BC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
      have hH_BC := on_line_of_between_ends hBHC hB_BC hC_BC
      have hBHA : Triangle B H A := Triangle.of_line hB_BC hH_BC
        (ne_of_between hBHC) (hABC.bca.off_line hB_BC hC_BC)
      have hCHA : Triangle C H A := Triangle.of_line hC_BC hH_BC
        (ne_of_between (between_symm hBHC)) (hABC.bca.off_line hB_BC hC_BC)
      obtain ⟨AH, hA_AH, hH_AH⟩ := Postulate1 A H hBHA.ne₂₃.symm
      -- Then, since BH is equal to EF, and AB to DE,
      -- the two sides AB, BH are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they contain
      -- equal angles;
      have hBA_ED : ‖B A‖ = ‖E D‖ :=
        (len_symm B A).trans (hAB.trans (len_symm D E))
      have hABH : ∠ A B H = ∠ D E F :=
        (angle_onRay_right (OnRay.of_between hBHC) hABC.ne₁₂).trans hB
      -- therefore the base AH is equal to the base DF,
      obtain ⟨hAH, harea, hA, hH⟩ := Prop4 hBHA.acb hDEF.bac hBA_ED hBH hABH
      -- and the triangle ABH is equal to the triangle DEF,
      have : △ A B H = △ D E F := by
        rw [area_swap A B H, area_rotate A H B, area_swap D E F, area_rotate D F E]
        exact harea
      -- and the remaining angles will be equal to the remaining angles, namely those which the
      -- equal sides subtend; [I. 4]
      have : ∠ B A H = ∠ E D F ∧ ∠ B H A = ∠ E F D := ⟨hA, hH⟩
      -- therefore the angle BHA is equal to the angle EFD.
      have hBHA_EFD : ∠ B H A = ∠ E F D := hH
      -- But the angle EFD is equal to the angle BCA;
      have hEFD : ∠ E F D = ∠ B C A := hC.symm
      -- therefore, in the triangle AHC, the exterior angle BHA is equal to the interior and
      -- opposite angle BCA:
      have hBHA_BCA : ∠ B H A = ∠ B C A := hBHA_EFD.trans hEFD
      -- which is impossible. [I. 16]
      have hless := (Prop16 hCHA.cab (between_symm hBHC)).1
      rw [angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_between (between_symm hBHC)) hABC.ne₁₃,
        angle_symm hBHA.ne₂₃.symm hBHA.ne₁₂, hBHA_BCA] at hless
      exact lt_irrefl _ hless
    -- Therefore BC is not unequal to EF,
    -- and is therefore equal to it.
    have hBC : ‖B C‖ = ‖E F‖ := by
      rcases lt_trichotomy ‖B C‖ ‖E F‖ with hlt | heq | hgt
      · exact False.elim (greater hDEF hABC hB.symm hC.symm hAB.symm hlt)
      · exact heq
      · exact False.elim (greater hABC hDEF hB hC hAB hgt)
    -- But AB is also equal to DE;
    -- therefore the two sides AB, BC are equal to the two sides DE, EF respectively, and they
    -- contain equal angles;
    have hBA_ED : ‖B A‖ = ‖E D‖ :=
      (len_symm B A).trans (hAB.trans (len_symm D E))
    -- therefore the base AC is equal to the base DF,
    obtain ⟨hAC, harea, hA, -⟩ := Prop4 hABC.bac hDEF.bac hBA_ED hBC hB
    -- the triangle ABC equal to the triangle DEF,
    have : △ A B C = △ D E F := by
      rw [area_swap A B C, area_rotate A C B, area_swap D E F, area_rotate D F E]
      exact harea
    -- and the remaining angle BAC equal to the remaining angle EDF. [I. 4]
    have hBAC : ∠ B A C = ∠ E D F := hA
    -- Therefore etc.
    exact ⟨hAB, hAC, hBC, hBAC⟩
  -- Q. E. D.
```

**Reading the figure**

- [`between_cases`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L74): Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two. (Between 6)
- [`between_of_between_left`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L66): If B is between A and C, and D is between A and B, then D is between A and C. (Between 4)
- [`between_of_between_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L70): If B is between A and C, and C is between B and D, then B is between A and D. (Between 5)
- [`between_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L43) (used here): If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1)
- [`centre_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L35): The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3)
- [`circles_meet`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L201): If each circle passes through a point inside the other, the circles cut one another. This is the step Euclid takes for granted in I.1. (Intersection 5)
- [`circles_meet_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L97): Two circles that cut one another do so on each side of the straight line through their centres. (Intersections 8)
- [`exists_point`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L28) (through [`Triangle.ne₁₂`](../../Elements/Figure/Triangles.lean#L22), [`Triangle.ne₁₃`](../../Elements/Figure/Triangles.lean#L36), [`Triangle.ne₂₃`](../../Elements/Figure/Triangles.lean#L29) and 1 other lemma): Let a point be taken. (Points 1)
- [`exists_point_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L40): Let a point be taken between B and C. (Points 3)
- [`exists_point_opposite_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L48): Let a point be taken on the other side of L from B. (Points 6)
- [`line_circle_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L85): A straight line through a point B inside a circle, heading out to a point C outside it, cuts the circle between B and C. (Intersections 4)
- [`line_circle_beyond`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L91): A straight line through a point B inside a circle, produced beyond B away from C, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5)
- [`line_unique`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L28) (through [`Triangle.of_line`](../../Elements/Figure/Triangles.lean#L82) and [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1)
- [`lines_meet_of_opposite_sides`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L179): A straight line joining points on opposite sides of L crosses L. (Intersection 1)
- [`ne_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L46) (used here): A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1)
- [`ne_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L49) (through [`OnRay.of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L32), [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108), [`angle_onRay_left`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L40) and 1 other lemma): The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L52) (through [`OnRay.of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L32)): If B is between A and C, then A is not between B and C. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L79): If B is between A and C, and also between A and D, then B is not between C and D: C and D lie on the same side of B. (Between 7)
- [`not_on_line_of_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L92): Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3)
- [`on_line_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L56): A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes through C. (Between 2)
- [`on_line_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L61) (used here): A straight line through A and C passes through every point between them. (Between 3)
- [`pasch2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L111) (through [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it again. (Pasch 2)
- [`pasch3`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L114): A straight line through a point between A and C separates them. (Pasch 3)
- [`pasch4`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L119): If two different straight lines L and M meet at B, and A and C are points of M, different from each other and from B, that are not on the same side of L, then B is between A and C. (Pasch 4)
- [`same_side_or`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L99): A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5)
- [`same_side_refl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L85): A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1)
- [`same_side_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L89) (through [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): If A is on the same side of a straight line as B, then B is on the same side as A. (Same side 2)
- [`same_side_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L96): Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same side as each other. (Same side 4)
- [`triple_incidence1`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L131): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A. If C lies within the angle BAD (on D's side of L and on B's side of N), then B and D are not on the same side of M: the straight line AC separates them. (Triple incidence 1)
- [`triple_incidence2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L139): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A, with B other than A and D off M. If C and D are on the same side of L, and B and D are not on the same side of M, then B and C are on the same side of N: C lies within the angle BAD. (Triple incidence 2)

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L54) (through [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): If D lies within the angle BAC, then BAC is made up of BAD and DAC. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L72) (through [`angle_onRay_left`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L40) and [`angle_onRay_right`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L47)): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L26) (used here): The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4)
- [`area_congruent`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L43): Triangles equal in all their sides and angles are equal in area. Euclid uses this without comment once he has shown two triangles congruent. (Metric 9)
- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L35) (used here): The triangle ABC is the triangle CAB. (Metric 8)
- [`area_swap`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L38) (used here): The triangle ABC is the triangle ACB. (Metric 8)
- [`eq_of_len_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L17): A finite straight line with distinct ends has length. (Metric 1)
- [`inside_of_len_lt`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L33): A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L21): If B is between A and C, then AB and BC together make up AC. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_lt_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L37): A point inside is nearer the centre than the circumference. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_self`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L20): The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1)
- [`len_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L23) (used here): The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3)
- [`same_ray_of_angle_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L49) (through [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): If the angle BAC is nothing, C lies on the ray from A through B. (Diagram-angle 1)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L30): **Superposition.** The triangle ABC can be applied to the straight line L with A on D, B on the ray from D through G, and C on the side of L where H is, without changing any side or angle.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L23): Adding three magnitudes in a row, it makes no difference whether the first two or the last two are added first. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L26) (through [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L45): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L29): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L32) (used here): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L35): What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L39) (used here): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L42) (through [`angle_lt_of_between`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L108)): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

_Our commentary: what Euclid assumes, what Lean made us say out loud, and how the result looks by modern means._

**Two cuts, two contradictions.** Euclid takes in turn the two places the equal side can stand. When it adjoins the equal angles, he supposes AB greater than DE and cuts off BG equal to DE: I.4 then makes the angle BCG equal to BCA, "the less to the greater". When it subtends one of them, he supposes BC greater than EF and cuts off BH equal to EF: I.4 now makes the exterior angle BHA equal to the interior and opposite angle BCA, which I.16 forbids. Either way the sides are equal, and I.4 finishes. Our figure, like Heath's, shows G and H together, though each has its own supposition.

**"The distance of ships in the sea."** Proclus tells a story: "Eudemus in his geometrical history refers this theorem to Thales. For he says that, in the method by which they say that Thales proved the distance of ships in the sea, it was necessary to make use of this theorem" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 304). Heath guesses that Thales stood on a tower with an upright stick and a cross-piece on a nail. He pointed the cross-piece at the ship, then turned the stick, still upright, until it pointed at a mark on the shore; the two triangles share the tower and the angles at its ends, so the mark was as far off as the ship (vol. 1, p. 305).

**Which is the greater?** Euclid lets AB be the greater, though it may as well be DE; we answer that by exchanging the triangles. In his figure G lies between B and A, and H between B and C, and that is what his contradictions need: BCG is then a part of BCA, and BHA an exterior angle of the triangle AHC. I.3 promises both when it cuts BG and BH off.

**An author unknown.** The other way to prove it, by applying one triangle to the other, "was very early discovered", Heath says, at least for the side adjoining the equal angles; an-Nairīzī gives it, "observing that the proof is one which he had found, but of which he did not know the author" (vol. 1, p. 303). Euclid's own proof moves nothing, and leaves superposition inside I.4.

**The modern way.** The sine rule, a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C, settles it at once: the two angles give the third, two right angles less their sum, and the one side then gives the other two. But the third angle comes from I.32, whose proof uses Postulate 5; Euclid's proof does without it.

## Further reading

- For the sine rule in the modern way, and where the sine itself came from, Glen Van Brummelen's [*The Mathematics of the Heavens and the Earth*](https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691129730/the-mathematics-of-the-heavens-and-the-earth) (2009) (also on [I.24](24.md)).
- For what Euclid proves without Postulate 5, as he proves this, Marvin Jay Greenberg's [*Euclidean and Non-Euclidean Geometries*](https://store.macmillanlearning.com/us/product/Euclidean-and-Non-Euclidean-Geometries/p/0716799480) (2008), ch. 4, "Neutral Geometry" (also on [I.16](16.md)).
